data.gender_notes: Ghumair is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘ghumr’, meaning ‘to be heavy’ or ‘burdened’. In Islamic context, it refers to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) who carried the burden of the entire nation on his shoulders. Ghumair is a noble and generous name for a boy, symbolizing strength and leadership. The name Ghumair carries the meaning “Noble, Generous” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghumair usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ghumair belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble, Generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghumair total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.context: The Banu Dhi l-Nun signed a peace treaty with Al-Mansur, the Almoravide Caliph, in 1010 CE, in which they agreed to pay tribute in exchange for protection from invading Christian forces. The treaty was sealed with a handshake between Ghumair ibn Abi Thabit, the Banu Dhi l-Nun leader, and Al-Mansur.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun, The History of the Berbers, Translated by P.R. Hitti, p. 324. The name Ghumair carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ghumair ibn Manzur was a Berber military leader who rebelled against the Marinids, the ruling dynasty of Morocco, in 1331 CE. He managed to gain the support of several powerful Berber tribes, and was able to capture the city of Fes before being defeated and killed in battle.
